new_statements.quote: Tsuvaɗi exhibits two level tones in its lexicon: High (H), Low (L), and one contour High-Low, or High-Falling (HL). All three can be observed in nouns with the noun class prefix hAC-, which consistently bears high tone [...] Automatic downdrifting also occurs word-internally [...] [p. 65] Out of 2000 words in the current data set, less than 1% of the words show minimal pair contrast for lexical tone. This shows that lexical tone has a very low load. [...] [p. 73] In Tsuvaɗi, all verbs exhibit grammatical tone and are lexically toneless. For disyllabic verb roots in the Realis mood, the verb takes a L-H.L melody on the index and root.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tsuvaɗi (of which 'Kakihum' kxe was a spurious duplicate entry) is described as a tone language with H, L and a HL contour, low lexical functional load and grammatical tone melodies on verbs; the sketch, the only modern phonological description, makes no statement about word stress or accent at all (the terms do not occur), nor does Blench's 2007 draft sketch.
new_statements.exceptions: None concerning stress. Tone: Low is realized as falling before pause (allotone); HL of the Irrealis melody surfaces as H sentence-medially.
new_statements.domain_note: Data are c. 2000 words mostly elicited in isolation (citation forms), Tsudugu (Azagaɗi) dialect; Kakihum/Agaɗi 'highlander' Tsuvaɗi belongs to the same eastern (Azagaɗi/Agaɗi) dialect grouping per Hansley et al. 2012 and Buttacavoli 2022:4-5.
new_statements.identity_note: kaki1247 'Kakihum' [kxe] is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid: ISO 639-3 CR 2014-040 retired it as a spurious duplicate and merged it into Tsuvadi [tvd] = Glottolog tsuv1239 (Kakihum town, Mariga LGA, hosts only Cicipu [awc, Ticuhũu dialect] and Tsuvaɗi; 'the Kakihum Tsuva'di seems to be more or less identical to the Tsuva'di spoken by Ava'di in the Tirisino and Tikula dialect areas'). Crozier & Blench 1992 / Blench & McGill 2012 Table 4 equate 'Agadi = Kakihum, people aGaɗi, language tsiGaɗi'; Hansley et al. 2012 write 'Kakihum (Agaɗi) [kxe]' and find Agaɗi ('highlander') speakers self-identify as Avaɗi speaking Tsuvaɗi, dialect Tsuvaɗi-Agaɗi. The quoted source (Buttacavoli 2022) describes the Tsudugu dialect, which belongs to the same eastern Azagaɗi ('highlanders') grouping; any catalog entry should be filed under tsuv1239 Tsuvadi rather than as a separate language, coded tonal with no stress statement.

sources.locator: Ch. 5 'Tones', sec. 5.1 Lexical Tone, p. 63 (p. 63); sec. 5.1.1 p. 65; sec. 5.2 Grammatical Tone, p. 73
sources.note: Tone-only analysis: ch. 5 Tones pp. 63-75 (two level lexical tones H, L plus HL contour; lexical tone 'has a very low load', p. 65; verbs lexically toneless with grammatical tone melodies, p. 73; automatic downdrift). Ch. 4 Syllable Structure pp. 50-62. The words stress/accent/prominence/intensity do not occur anywhere in the text; no statement on word stress. Pp. 4-5: Kakihum is 'actually a village where both Cicipu and Tsuvaɗi are spoken'; dialect groups Azagaɗi (east, 'highlanders') vs Azozolo; focus dialect Tsudugu is Azagaɗi.
Retired entry, merged into Tsuvadi [tvd] per CR 2014-040; only reference is the change request.

sources.note: Sec. 3.3 Tones p. 5: 'it seems clear from his transcription that he takes the system to be high, low and falling.. This also seems to be the system of TsuVaɗi.. The tone of nominal prefixes is driven by the stem in all cases, while the tones of verbs seem to reflect the numbers of syllables.' No mention of stress or accent.
Lists Kakihum (Gadi, Gaɗi) as a dialect [citation needed]; consonant/vowel tables from Buttacavoli 2022 and Blench 2007; nothing on tone or stress.
